sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:193655
Court No. - 66
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 44420 of 2024

Applicant :- Suraj Kumar Verma
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Sanjay Kumar Sharma
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Sanjay Kumar Sharma, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Jhamman Ram,
learned AGA-I, for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.11 of 2023, under Sections 411 and 420 IPC and Section 66D I.T.Act,
Police Station Cyber Crime, District Moradabad during pendency of the trial.

entities.text: Police Station Cyber Crime, District Moradabad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
3. FIR of the present case was lodged against Agent Adarsh and according to the FIR by playing fraud more than Rs.Fifteen Lacs of the informant have been duped by Agent Adarsh.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant was not named in the FIR and during investigation he has been made accused in the present matter and admittedly applicant was not the person, who duped the informant and neither he misappropriated the amount nor any money was transferred in his account.
Suraj Kumar Verma vs State Of U.P. on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132802329/
1 5.

entities.text: Suraj Kumar Verma vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that during investigation co-accused Ankit Chaudhary, Bhupendra Singh Chauhan and Jai Kumar Vishwakarma were also made accused and all the three co-accused have been released on bail by this Court and their bail order has been annexed as Anneure-8 to the affidavit filed in support of the instant bail application.

6. He further submits that applicant is the student and he is not having any previous criminal history and all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate with maximum punishment of seven years and applicant is in jail in the present matter since 12.2.2024, i.e., for the last more than nine months.
7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. However, there is allegation that applicant along with other co-accused persons duped the informant and misappropriated his Rs.Fourteen Lacs but all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate with maximum punishment of seven years.
10.
Further, three co-accused persons Ankit Chaudhary, Bhupendra Singh Chauhan and Jai Kumar Vishwakarma have already been released on bail by this Court.
11. Further, applicant is in jail in the present matter since 12.2.2024, i.e., for the last more than nine months.

12. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
13. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant-Suraj Kumar Verma be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.

16. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
